cards.explanation: The answer is Edom. The passage says Mount Hor sits "…near the border of the land of Edom…" (Numbers 20:23). So Edom is the land by that mountain, friends, and I didn't even have to stamp it into anybody's hand.

The answer is False. God says Aaron "…will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites…" (Numbers 20:24). The land is given to the Israelites, but Aaron won't walk into it. I think that's a heavy line, friends.

The answer is that they rebelled against His command. God says "…both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah." (Numbers 20:24). Notice God says both of them, friends. He's talking to Moses and Aaron together, and that's the reason He gives for Aaron not entering the land.

The answer is Eleazar, friends! God says, "Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor." (Numbers 20:25). Eleazar is the one who goes up the mountain with them. And hang onto that name, because the next verse says what Eleazar will wear.

The answer is his priestly garments. God says, "Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar." (Numbers 20:26). The garments go from Aaron to Eleazar. It's like handing over the apron, friends, and I'll tell you, mine has seen some flour.

The answer is True. The text says they climbed Mount Hor "…in the sight of the whole congregation." (Numbers 20:27). So the whole congregation is in a position to see the three of them go up. That's a lot of eyes on one mountain, friends, and I get nervous when two people watch me stamp.
The answer is Moses and Eleazar. "Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain." (Numbers 20:28). Three went up and two come down, friends. I think that's a quiet walk, and I'll leave it quiet.

The answer is that they mourn for him thirty days. The text says "…the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days." (Numbers 20:29). That's the whole house of Israel, friends, not just a few people. Thirty days is a real stretch of time, and I think that tells us Aaron mattered to them.
